Ali bin Sahl told me: Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Burqan, on the authority of Yazid, regarding this verse, And do not turn your cheek away from people, he said: If someone speaks to you, turn your face away from him, looking down on him. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Khalid bin Hayyan Al-Raqi told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Maymun bin Mihran, who said: It is a man who speaks to another man and turns his face away. Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad told us: Muhammad ibn Rabi’ah told us: Abu Makin told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And do not turn your cheek away from people, he said: Do not turn your face away. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning: Do not turn away from people, meaning: Turn your face towards people and show good character. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And do not turn your cheek away from people, he said: Turning the cheek away means being arrogant and haughty towards people and belittling them. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Makin, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Turning away. Others said: He only forbade him from doing that to someone who was close to him, not out of arrogance. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And do not turn your cheek away from people. He said: A man has envy between him and his brother, and he sees it and turns away from him. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not turn your cheek away from people, he said: It is the man who has a grudge against his brother and turns away from him. Others said: It is the emphasis. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me, on the authority of Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: It is the clenching of the jaw. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: It is the emphasis or the emphasis Al-Tabari is in doubt. Yahya bin Talha told us: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, with a similar narration. And His saying, And do not walk on the earth exultantly, means: Do not walk on the earth arrogantly. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, And do not walk upon the earth exultantly, that he said: with arrogance. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “And do not turn your cheek toward people and do not walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, God does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful.” He said: He forbade him from being arrogant. His statement, Indeed, God does not like everyone self-deluded, is arrogant and boastful. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Every arrogant boaster, he said: Arrogant. And his statement, Proud, he said: He enumerates what God has given, but he does not thank God.
31:19: He says: Be humble in your walk when you walk, do not be arrogant, and do not rush, but take your time. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, except that some of them said: He ordered him to be humble in his walking, and some of them said: He ordered him to stop being quick in it. It was mentioned that he ordered him to be humble in his walk. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid: And be moderate in your walking. He said: Humility. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And be moderate in your walking. He said: He forbade him from being arrogant. Mention of those who said: He forbade him from speeding. Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, regarding His statement, And be moderate in your pace, he said: from speed. His statement, And lower your voice, he said: Lower your voice, and make it moderate when you speak. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And lower your voice. He said: He ordered him to be moderate in his voice. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And lower your voice, he said: Lower your voice. The commentators differed in their interpretation of his statement, The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. Some of them said: Its meaning is: The most disagreeable of sounds. Who said that? Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah and Aban bin Taghlib, who said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: The most disagreeable of sounds he said: The most disagreeable of sounds is the sound of donkeys. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. That is, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys, its beginning is a sigh and its end is an inhalation. He ordered him to be moderate in his voice. Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us: I heard Al-A’mash say: The most disagreeable of sounds is the sound of donkeys. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The worst of sounds. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Wadh, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, The most disagreeable of voices they said: The most evil of voices. Jabir said: Al-Hasan bin Muslim said: The loudest voices. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys, he said: If raising one’s voice was good, He would not have made it for donkeys. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: It means: the ugliest or most evil of voices. This is similar to what they say when they see an ugly face or a hideous sight: How ugly is so-and-so’s face, and how ugly is his sight. As for his saying, the sound of donkeys, the sound, which is one, is added to the donkeys, which are a group. This is for two reasons. If you wish, you can say: The sound means the group, as it was said, He would have taken away their hearing (al-Baqarah 2:20). If you wish, you can say: The meaning of donkeys is the meaning of the one, because the one in such a situation represents the group.
31:20: God Almighty says, Have you not seen, O people, that God has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens of the sun, moon, stars, and clouds and whatever is on the earth of animals, trees, water, seas, ships, and other benefits? All of this is for your benefit and interests, for your food, sustenance, provisions, and refuge. You enjoy some of all of it and benefit from all of it. And He has bestowed upon you His blessings, both apparent and hidden. The reciters differed in their reading of this. Some of the Meccans and most of the Kufians read it and He bestowed upon you His blessings as the singular, and they interpreted its meaning to mean Islam, or to mean the testimony that there is no god but God. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as Ni’mah as the plural, and they interpreted its meaning to mean the blessings that God has subjected to His servants from what is in the heavens and the earth. They cited as evidence for the correctness of their reading the words grateful for His blessings (al-Nahl 16:121). They said: This is the plural of blessings. The correct statement in our view is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, and they have close meanings. This is because blessing may mean a single word, or a group, and group may include a single word. God, the Most High, said: {And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them} (Ibrahim 14:34), so it is known that He did not mean a single blessing. And He said elsewhere: {And he was not among the polytheists grateful for His favors}, so He made them plural. So whichever of the two readings the reciter recites that with, he is correct. Some of those who read it mentioned monotheism, and interpreted it as we mentioned about its readers that they interpret it. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Mastour Al-Hana’i told me, on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he read it And He has bestowed upon you His favor, apparent and hidden, and Islam interpreted it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’, who said: Sharik bin Abdullah narrated on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he read blessing as one. He said: If it had been blessings, it would have been a blessing less than a blessing, or a blessing above a blessing the doubt is from Al-Farra’. Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told me, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: Hamid told us, he said: Mujahid recited And He has bestowed upon you His favor, apparent and hidden, he said: There is no god but God. Al-Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, he said: Ibn Abi Bakr told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid And He has bestowed upon you His favor, apparent and hidden, he said: He used to say: It is there is no god but God. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hamid Al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid And He has bestowed upon you His favor, both apparent and hidden, he said: There is no god but God. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hamid Al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: There is no god but God. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Ibn Abbas a blessing that is apparent and hidden, he said: There is no god but God. And his saying apparent means: apparent on the tongues in words, and on the bodies and limbs of the body in actions. And his saying and hidden means: and hidden in the hearts in belief and knowledge. And His statement, And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge or guidance, God Almighty says: And among the people is he who disputes about the Oneness of God, and sincere obedience and worship of Him, without knowledge of what he disputes about, nor guidance: He says: Nor a statement with which to clarify the truth of what he says, nor an illuminating book, He says: Nor a revelation from God that brought what he claims, clarifying the truth of his claim. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book. He has no proof or Book from God.
31:21: God Almighty says: And when it is said to those who dispute about the Oneness of God out of ignorance of the greatness of God: “O people, follow what God has revealed to His Messenger and believe in it, for it distinguishes between those among us who are right and those who are wrong, and separates between those who are astray and those who are guided,” and they say: Rather, we follow the religions that we found our fathers following, for they were people of truth, God Almighty says: Or even if Satan were to invite them by making their evil deeds appear attractive to them, and their following him in their misguidance, and their disbelief in God and their abandonment of following what God has revealed of His Book to His Prophet to the punishment of the Blazing Fire, meaning: the punishment of the blazing fire that is blazing and raging.
31:22: God Almighty says: And whoever worships His Face, humbly submitting to Him in worship, acknowledging His divinity, and is a doer of good, meaning: and he is obedient to God in His commands and prohibitions, has grasped the most trustworthy handhold, meaning: he has grasped the most trustworthy end, the end of which he does not fear breaking if he holds on to it. This is an example, and what he means by that is that he has grasped the pleasure of God by submitting to Him and is a doer of good, such that he does not fear the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu al-Sawda’, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And whoever submits his face to God while he is a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. He said: There is no god but God. His saying, And to God is the outcome of all matters, means: To God is the outcome of every matter, good and bad, and He is the One who will question its people about it and reward them for it.
31:23: God Almighty says: And whoever disbelieves in God, let not his disbelief grieve you, nor let your soul be consumed with regret over them, for indeed, their return and destiny on the Day of Resurrection is to Us, and We will inform them of their evil deeds that they did in this world, then We will recompense them for them with their due recompense. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. He says: Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what their breasts conceal of disbelief in God and preference for obeying Satan.
31:24: And His statement, We grant them enjoyment for a little while, means: We grant them respite in this world for a little while in which they may enjoy themselves. Then We will force them to a severe punishment, means: Then We will bring them, against their will, to a severe punishment, and that is the punishment of the Fire. We seek refuge in God from it, and from any action that brings one closer to it.
31:25: God Almighty says: And if you, O Muhammad, ask these polytheists among your people, Who created the heavens and the earth? they will surely say, God. Say, Praise be to God. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad: So if they say that, then say to them, Praise be to God who created that, not to the One who does not create anything and is created. Then God Almighty says, But most of them do not know. He says: Rather, most of these polytheists do not know who is to be praised, and where the place of thanks lies.
31:26: And His statement, To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, God Almighty says: To God belongs everything in the heavens and the earth, whatever that thing may be, whether an idol or a statue or anything else, whether worshipped or not. Indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, meaning: God is the Free of need of the worship of these polytheists, idols and rivals to Him, and anything else from them and from all of His creation, because they are His property and His, and they have a need for Him. The Praiseworthy means the One who is praised for His blessings that He has bestowed upon His creation.
31:27: God Almighty says: And if all the trees of the earth were to be turned into pens, and the sea were to replenish it. He says: The sea has ink. The ha in His statement replenishes it refers to the sea. And His statement: After him will be seven more seas, the Words of God would not be exhausted. In this statement there is an omission that is dispensed with by the apparent meaning of it, which is that the Word of God is written with those pens and that ink, so those pens would be broken, and that ink would be exhausted, but the Words of God would not be exhausted. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I asked Al-Hasan about this verse, And if all the trees on the earth were pens, he said: If the trees of the earth were pens, and the seas were ink, and God said: Indeed, such and such is part of My affair, and such and such is part of My affair, the water of the seas would be exhausted, and the pens would be broken. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Al-Hakam told us, he said: Amr told us, regarding his statement, And if all the trees on the earth were pens, he said: If pens were sharpened and the sea were ink, and it was written with those pens from it, The Words of God would not be exhausted, even if it were for a period of seven ahraz. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were replenished thereafter by seven more seas, the Words of God would not be exhausted. He said: The polytheists said: This is only speech that is about to be exhausted. He said: If the trees of the land were pens, and the sea were seven seas, the wonders of my Lord, His wisdom, His creation, and His knowledge, would not be exhausted. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a result of an argument that the Jews had with him. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: A man from the people of Mecca narrated to me, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “The Jewish rabbis said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina: ‘O Muhammad, do you think that His statement, “And of knowledge you have been given only a little” Al-Isra’ 17:85 does he mean us or your people?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No.’ They said: ‘Do you not recite in what came to you: ‘We have been given the Torah, in which is clarification of all things.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is little in the knowledge of God, and you have what is sufficient for you.’ So God revealed to him regarding what they had asked him about in this regard: ‘And if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were replenished thereafter by seven more seas, the Words of God would not be exhausted.’’ That is, the Torah is little in this regard from God’s knowledge. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The People of the Book asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the spirit, so God revealed: {And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord. And of knowledge you have not been given except a little.} (al-Isra’ 17:85) They said: You claim that we have only been given a little knowledge, but we have been given the Torah, which is wisdom. {And whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good.} (al-Baqarah 2:269) He said: Then the verse was revealed: {If all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were ink, and seven more seas were replenished thereafter, the Words of God could not be exhausted.} He said: Whatever knowledge you have been given, by which God has saved you from the Fire and admitted you to Paradise, it is abundant and good, but in comparison to the knowledge of God it is little. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, who said: “When the verse And of the knowledge you have been given only a little (al-Isra’ 17:95) was revealed in Mecca, meaning the Jews, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, the Jewish rabbis came to him and said: O Muhammad, have we not heard that you say And of the knowledge you have been given only a little (al-Isra’ 17:85), do you mean us or your people? He said: No, you do mean it. They said: You recite: We have been given the Torah, and in it is the clarification of everything. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is little compared to the knowledge of God, and God has given you that which, if you acted upon it, you would benefit from. Then God revealed: And if whatever trees on the earth were pens and the sea were ink, to be replenished thereafter by seven more seas…” until His saying: Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And the sea, replenished thereafter by seven more seas. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited al-Bahr in the nominative case as the subject, while the reciters of Basra recited it in the accusative case, in apposition to ma in His statement, And if all that is on the earth were, and whichever of the two the reciter recites, he is correct in my opinion. And His statement, Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise, means: Indeed, God is Exalted in Might in His vengeance against those who associate partners with Him and claim a god other than Him, and is Wise in His management of His creation.
31:28: God Almighty says: “You, O people, are not created and are not resurrected by God except as the creation of a single soul and its resurrection. That is because nothing that God wills is impossible for Him, and nothing that He desires is prevented from Him. “His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.” (Ya-Sin 36:82) So it is the same whether He creates one person and resurrects him, or He creates and resurrects all of them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, like a single soul, meaning: Be and it is, for little and much. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul, he said: He says: God created all people and resurrected them like the creation of a single soul and resurrected it. It is only appropriate to say: except as a single soul, and the meaning is: except as the creation of a single soul, because the omitted word is a verb indicated by his statement, He did not create you and resurrect you, and the Arabs do that in verbal nouns, and from that is the statement of God, Their eyes will roll like one who faints from death (al-Ahzab 33:19). The meaning is: like the rolling of the eye of one who faints from death, so the rolling and the eye were not mentioned because of what they were described. And His statement, Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, means that God Almighty says: Indeed, God is All-Hearing of what these polytheists say and fabricate about their Lord, from their claiming that He has partners and equals and other words of theirs and the words of others. He is All-Seeing of what they and other people do, and He will reward them for that with their reward.
31:29: God Almighty says, Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with your own eyes, that God merges the night into the day meaning: He increases the hours of the night’s deficiency into the hours of the day. And merges the day into the night meaning: He increases the hours of the day’s deficiency into the hours of the night. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Have you not seen that God merges the night into the day? means the decrease of the night into the increase of the day. And He merges the day into the night. means the decrease of the day into the increase of the night. And His statement, And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term, God Almighty says: And He has subjected the sun and the moon for the interests and benefits of His creation, each running: He says: All of that runs by His command until a specified time, and a limited term when it reaches it, He rolled up the sun and the moon. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term, meaning: for all of this there is a time and a known limit, which it does not exceed or transgress. And His statement, And that God is Acquainted with what you do, means: And God, O people, is All-Aware of your deeds, whether good or evil. Nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of it. This statement was addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the intended meaning is the polytheists. That is because God, the Most High, pointed out with His statement, Indeed, God merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, the point of His argument from ignorance of His greatness, and associating others with Him in worship. This is indicated by His statement, That is because God is the Truth, and that which they invoke besides Him is falsehood.
31:30: God the Most High says: This that I have informed you, O Muhammad, that God did by combining the night into the day, and the day into the night, and other than that from His great power, and He only did it because He is truly God, not what these polytheists call upon Him to do, and that no one is able to do that except Him, and divinity is only suitable for the One who does that with His power. And His statement, And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, the Most High says: And that what these polytheists distance besides God is falsehood that fades away, perishes, and is destroyed. And that God is the Most High, the Grand, the Most High says: And that God is the Most High, meaning: He who is lofty over everything, and everything below Him is humbled and submissive to Him. The Great to whom everything below Him is humbled and submissive.
31:31: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you not see, O Muhammad, that ships sail the sea as a blessing from God to His creation? “To show you some of His signs meaning: To show you some of His lessons and His proofs against you. Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful person. He says: In the ships sailing the sea, there is evidence that God, who made them sail, is the Truth, and that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood. For every patient, grateful person. He says: For everyone who is patient with himself and does not abstain from what God has forbidden, and thanks Him for His blessings and does not deny Him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Mutraf used to say: Among the servants of God most beloved to Him are the patient and grateful. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, who said: Patience is half of faith, gratitude is half of faith, and certainty is all of faith. Have you not seen His statement: Indeed in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful. Indeed in that are signs for those of certainty. (Indeed in that are signs for the believers.) Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. He said: Patience is half of faith, and certainty is all of faith. If someone were to ask: How did He specify that this evidence is for the patient and grateful, and not for the rest of creation? It would be said: Because patience and gratitude are among the actions of those with wisdom and intellect. So He informed us that in this are signs for every rational being, because God made these signs a lesson for those with intellects and discernment.
31:32: God Almighty says: And when those whom they invoke other than God, gods and idols, at sea, when they embark on ships, are covered by waves like shadows, which is the plural of shadow, and the waves are likened to it in the intensity of the blackness of the abundance of water. Nabigha of Banu Ja'dah said in describing the sea: Green with shades on its edges, the cracks of the jugs He likened the wave, which is one, to shadows, which are a group, because the wave comes one part after another, and some of it rides on others like the form of shadows. And His statement, Call upon God, making your religion sincere to Him, means, “And when a wave like shadows covers these people, and they fear drowning, they resort to God in supplication, making their obedience sincere to Him, not associating anything with Him there, nor calling upon anyone besides Him, nor seeking help from anyone other than Him.” His statement, Then when He delivered them to the land, from what they feared in the sea of drowning and destruction, to the land, then some of them are moderate, means, Some of them are moderate in their speech and their acknowledgment of their Lord, while at the same time concealing disbelief in Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And among them is he who is moderate, he said: He is moderate in speech, but he is a disbeliever. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And among them is he who is moderate, he said: The moderate is the one who is on the right path in the matter. And His statement, And none denies Our signs except every traitor and ungrateful person, God Almighty says: And none denies Our proofs and arguments except every traitor to his covenant. And treachery among the Arabs is the ugliest form of treachery, and from this is the saying of Amr ibn Ma’di Karib: If you had seen Abu Umair, you would have filled your hands with treachery and deceit. His saying ungrateful means: ungrateful for blessings, not grateful for the blessings bestowed upon him. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of chosen one, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Every traitor is ungrateful. He said: Every treacherous person. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Every traitor, he said: A traitor. Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And none denies Our signs except every traitor and ungrateful person, he said: A traitor. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And none denies Our signs except every traitor and ungrateful person. The traitor is the treacherous person, every traitor with his pledge is ungrateful to his Lord. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And none denies Our signs except every traitor and ungrateful person, he said: Every denier is ungrateful. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Hab told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And none denies Our signs except every deceiver and ungrateful, he said: Deceitful is the traitor, just as you say: He betrayed me. Ibn Kay` told us: My father told us, on the authority of Mis`ar, who said: I heard Qatada say: He who betrays his covenant. He said: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: The traitor. He said: My father told us: On the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shamir bin Atiyah Al-Kahili, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Deceit is treachery, and treachery is disbelief.
31:33: God Almighty says: O polytheists of Quraysh, fear God and fear that His wrath will descend upon you on a day when no father can avail his son, nor can a son avail his father at all, because the matter will then be in the hands of the One who cannot be overcome, and intercession and means will be of no use with Him, except a means from the good deeds that he did in the past in this world. And His statement, Indeed, the promise of God is true, means: Know that the coming of this day is true, and that is because God has promised His servants and He does not break His promise. So let not the worldly life deceive you, means: Do not let the adornments and pleasures of this worldly life deceive you, so that you incline toward it and neglect to prepare for what will save you from God’s punishment on that day. And His statement, And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God, means: Do not let a Deceiver deceive you about God. Deceit, with the opening of the ghain, is whatever deceives a person, be it a devil, a human being, or the world. As for deceit, with the closing of the ghain, it is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: I deceived him with deceit. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning God, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Deception, he said: Satan. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning God, that is Satan. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid Al-Marwazi, who said: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, Delusion, he said: Satan. Some of them interpreted arrogance as: Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Dinar, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement, And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning God, he said: That you commit a sin and hope for forgiveness.
31:34: God Almighty says: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. He will come to you with the knowledge of His coming to you from your Lord. No one knows when He will come to you. He will not come to you except suddenly, so fear Him, lest He surprise you suddenly while you are still in your misguidance and have not repented from it, and you will become from the torment and punishment of God to that which you cannot bear. And God Almighty began the report of His knowledge of the coming of the Hour. The meaning is what I mentioned, because the speech indicates what is intended by it. He said, Indeed, with God is knowledge of the Hour, in which the Resurrection will take place, no one else knows that. And He sends down the rain, from the sky, no one else has power over that. And He knows what is in the wombs, the wombs of females. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, meaning, And no living soul knows what it will do tomorrow, “And no soul knows in what land it will die,” meaning, And no living soul knows in what land its end will be. “Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted,” meaning, the One who knows all of that is God, not anyone else. He has knowledge of everything, nothing is hidden from Him. He is Acquainted with what is and what has been. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He said: “A man came - Abu Ja`far said: I think it was me, he said - to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My wife is pregnant, so tell me what she will give birth to? Our land is barren, so tell me when the rain will fall. I know when she gave birth, so tell me when I will die. So God revealed: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain”... to the end of the Surah.” He said: So Mujahid used to say: They are the keys of the unseen of which God said: “And with Him are the keys of the unseen. None knows them except Him” (Al-An`am: 59). Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour… the verse, things from the unseen, God has kept them to Himself, and He has not informed any close angel or sent prophet about them. Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour so no one among the people knows when the Hour will come, in which year, or in which month, or night, or day. And He sends down the rain so no one knows when the rain will come, whether it comes by night or day. And He knows what is in the wombs so no one knows what is in the wombs, male or female, red or black, or what it is. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow good or evil. And you do not know, O son of Adam, when you will die. Perhaps you will die tomorrow, perhaps you will be afflicted tomorrow. And no soul knows in what land it will die No one among the people knows where his resting place is on earth, whether at sea or on land, or in a plain or a mountain. Exalted and Blessed is He. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Aisha said: Whoever says that anyone knows the unseen except God has lied and made a great slander against God. God said: None in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God (al-Naml 27:65). Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, “That a man said: O Messenger of God, is there any knowledge that you have not been given? He said: You have been given much knowledge, and good knowledge, or something like that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain’… to ‘Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted’. None knows them except God, Blessed and Exalted be He.” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn Muhammad told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The keys of the unseen are five. Then he recited these verses: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour... to the end of it. Ali ibn Sahl told me, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, that he heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The keys of the unseen are five, and none knows them but God: ‘Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs.’ … the verse. Then he said: ‘No one knows what will happen tomorrow but God, and no one knows when the rain will send down but God, and no one knows when the Hour will come but God, and no one knows what is in the wombs but God, and no soul knows in what land it will die.’” Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The keys of the unseen are five, and none knows them but God: God has knowledge of the Hour, sends down the rain, and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. God is Knowing and Acquainted.” Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abd God ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Everything was given to your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except the five knowledge of the unseen: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die.” Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Whoever tells you that he knows what will happen tomorrow has lied. Then she recited: And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow. He said: Jarir and Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Khabab, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There are five things that no one knows except God: ‘Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain’… the verse.” Abu Sharhabil told me: Abu Al-Yaman told us: Ismail told us, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Everything that has been given to your Prophet except the five keys of the unseen, then he recited this verse: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour... to the end. And it was said: In what land will you die? And in another language: In what land. So whoever says: In what land, the feminine of the earth is sufficient so that it does not appear in any other femininity. And whoever says In what land and feminizes: that is, he said: It may be sufficient with any of what it is added to, so the feminine is necessary, like when someone says: I passed by a woman, and it is said to him: In what way, and I passed by a man, and it is said to him: In what way, and it is said: Which woman came to you and he came to you, and which woman came to you.
